title: First baths — sponge bath until the cord falls off
summary: Newborns do not need daily baths. Gentle sponge baths keep the cord dry.
whatsNormal:
Until the umbilical stump falls off:

• Sponge baths only — wipe face, neck folds, hands, and diaper area
• Keep stump dry; fold diaper below it
• 2–3 baths per week is enough for most healthy newborns
• Warm room, warm water, never leave baby unattended on a high surface

After the stump falls off and the belly button heals, short tub baths are fine — support head and neck throughout.
watchFor: Chilling: blue lips, mottled skin, or weak cry after bath
Soap in eyes causing lasting redness
Cord stump getting soaked or smelly
Dry, cracked skin from too-frequent bathing
callDoctorIf: Cord redness, pus, or bleeding — see umbilical cord care guide
Rash or irritation that worsens after bathing products
Baby seems to struggle breathing during or after bath
You want product recommendations for sensitive newborn skin
